principles: _hash invariance above all: a mass write to ~190 findings.json must change ZERO finding _hash.
Audit-only provenance: signatureTag + signatureTagSource never touch signFinding/_hash/any gate.
Deterministic + auditable: consume a committed signature map, no LLM at runtime.
Safe by default: dry-run default, --apply explicit, idempotent, only-empty-filled, never overwrite confirmed.
Pure decision leaf + thin store-adapter handler.
drivers: Persist the 3.5-proven signatures into the live base so learning_scan/hints/learning_effectiveness use real data.
Never perturb the finding _hash or the REVIEW->TEST findings gate across the touched stories.
Keep the reviewed diff small: build+test the command; mass-apply is a post-DONE operation.

options.name: Command consuming a committed map, dry-run default, _hash-safe attach (chosen)
pros: Reuses the proven _hash-excluded attach pattern; zero _hash change
dry-run default + idempotent = safe mass write
small reviewed diff; mass-apply is a separate operation
cons: Requires the map to be generated separately (already done in 3.5)

options.name: Command re-runs the LLM per finding
cons: Non-deterministic, non-auditable, slow, network-dependent; cannot be hermetically tested

options.name: Direct one-off script writing findings.json
cons: Bypasses the Lattice audit/review; risky un-reviewed mass write; no reusable/idempotent tool

chosen: Command consuming a committed map, dry-run default, _hash-safe attach (chosen)
rationale: A reviewed, deterministic command that consumes the committed 3.5 map and reuses the existing _hash-excluded attach pattern is the only safe way to mass-write signatures into ~190 findings without perturbing any finding _hash or gate; dry-run default + idempotency make the operation safe and repeatable, and keeping the actual apply as a post-DONE operation keeps the reviewed diff small. Re-running the LLM or a raw script would be non-deterministic/un-auditable or un-reviewed.

preMortem.scenario: The mass write changes finding _hash and breaks the findings gate.
preMortem.trigger: signatureTag/signatureTagSource get included in the object signFinding hashes, or writeFindings reserializes in a way that perturbs _hash.
preMortem.consequence: Every touched finding's signature changes; the REVIEW->TEST findings gate breaks across ~190 stories.
preMortem.mitigation: Attach the two fields AFTER _hash exactly as finding.ts does; recompute nothing hashed; the smoke asserts the finding _hash is byte-identical before/after via real signFinding for every touched finding (THE critical check).
Fill only when current tag is empty (or 'auto' with --overwriteAuto); never 'confirmed'; the smoke asserts confirmed=untouched.

preMortem.scenario: An accidental apply corrupts live data.
preMortem.trigger: The command writes by default without --apply, or is non-idempotent.
preMortem.mitigation: Dry-run is the DEFAULT (writes nothing); --apply required; idempotent (second apply = no change); the smoke asserts dry-run writes nothing + idempotency.

preMortem.consequence: Full npm test fails at DONE.
preMortem.mitigation: Add the L2 experience-layer entry; verifier runs full npm test; run npm test before REVIEW.
